messages.author: 8baccea4a1abda30
messages.subject: Rstanarm without covmat?
parts: I'm fitting multilevel models with ca 25k random effects, using rstanarm. R then simply got stuck. Looking around a bit I saw that stan_glmer returns the variance-covariance matrix of the coefficients ("covmat") element that already with a model fit on a fifth of my data it is 800MB. It seems I don't have not enough RAM for that model fit on the full data. Is there a way to call stan_glmer without producing the covmat? And also, shouldn't most people be ok with just getting the posterior samples?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Rstanarm without covmat?
parts:
On Monday, May 23, 2016 at 8:56:38 AM UTC-4, juliansc...@aol.com wrote:
I'm fitting multilevel models with ca 25k random effects, using rstanarm. R then simply got stuck. Looking around a bit I saw that stan_glmer returns the variance-covariance matrix of the coefficients ("covmat") element that already with a model fit on a fifth of my data it is 800MB. It seems I don't have not enough RAM for that model fit on the full data. Is there a way to call stan_glmer without producing the covmat? And also, shouldn't most people be ok with just getting the posterior samples?

Most people, yes, but things like the covariance matrix are needed for some post-estimation methods to work the same way as they do with glmer. In this case, we should probably just calculate the covariance among the common parameters. I'll try to fix this before we release a new rstanarm tomorrow.

Ben
